### How this work is cited

Passages inside Ḥayy ibn Yaqẓān are identified by section of the narrative. A philosophical fable about a man raised alone on an island who arrives by reason alone at the truths the religious tradition teaches. Ibn Tufayl's point is not that revelation is unnecessary but that the two paths converge — and Ibn Rushd's Decisive Treatise, also in this archive, argues the same question in legal form.

### The work in Ibn Tufayl’s thought

Ibn Ṭufayl (c. 1105–1185) was an Andalusian physician and vizier best known for the philosophical romance Ḥayy ibn Yaqẓān. [More on Ibn Tufayl](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ibn-tufayl) .
